earlier_claim: The region has a history far older than the state formed in 1956.
corrected_treatment: Retain, distinguishing planetary, geological, archaeological and administrative histories.

earlier_claim: Edakkal engravings date to around 6000 BCE.
corrected_treatment: Record 6000 BCE as the tourism page’s attribution, not an established absolute date.

earlier_claim: Edakkal establishes people living there about 8000 years ago.
corrected_treatment: This calculation inherits the unverified 6000 BCE premise; do not make it a dated occupation fact.

earlier_claim: Edakkal is the oldest widely cited prehistoric evidence / an appropriate earliest-human start.
corrected_treatment: No bibliometric oldest-widely-cited ranking was established. Investigate earlier stone-tool evidence independently.

earlier_claim: Edakkal is a cave in Wayanad.
corrected_treatment: The conventional place name is retained; the physical setting is a natural rock shelter/cleft, not necessarily a solution cave.

earlier_claim: Its pictures depict humans, animals, symbols and everyday activities.
corrected_treatment: Human/animal-like forms and signs can be catalogued; everyday activity and meaning are interpretations, not automatically identifiable facts.

earlier_claim: The engravings belong to different periods.
corrected_treatment: Multiple additions are a scholarly interpretation; panel-by-panel dates are not supplied by this audit.

earlier_claim: Earlier human activity than Edakkal is possible.
corrected_treatment: The 2016 abstract is a concrete lead to reported Lower Palaeolithic evidence; it does not determine the first occupation date.

earlier_claim: Ashoka’s inscriptions provide a third-century BCE documentary anchor.
corrected_treatment: Retain as an early external reference, not proof of the earliest conceivable record about any place inside the territory.

earlier_claim: Approximately 250 BCE is a firm starting point.
corrected_treatment: Use a third-century horizon. The inspected translator proposes 257 BCE; retain that as attributed dating, not a universal exact start.

earlier_claim: Keralaputra / Kedalaputo are interchangeable exact transcriptions.
corrected_treatment: Preserve witness-specific spellings and scripts. Compare critical editions before normalizing all forms.

earlier_claim: Keralaputras are generally associated with Cheras.
corrected_treatment: Do not translate this conventional identification into proof of exact territory, dynasty chronology or modern identity. The full identification literature has not been audited.

earlier_claim: The Ashokan reference establishes Mauryan control of Kerala.
corrected_treatment: The inspected Edict II translation names these peoples beyond the ruler’s borders; do not infer annexation.

earlier_claim: Sangam literature can be used to reconstruct early Chera history.
corrected_treatment: Collect individual poems, editions, layers, proposed dates and place identifications. The corpus was not verified in this pass.

earlier_claim: Sangam poems provide exact event dates or a single compositional date.
corrected_treatment: No such precision was justified. Keep text composition, redaction and surviving witness separate.

earlier_claim: The Periplus is a first-century CE Greek-language trade account.
corrected_treatment: The inspected edition supports the general period and port/trade content. No exact composition year adopted.

earlier_claim: Pliny gives relevant Kerala-coast evidence.
corrected_treatment: A relevant Natural History VI.26 lead was located, but the primary passage was not inspected. Do not mark this subclaim fully verified.

earlier_claim: Ptolemy’s work is relevant to the second-century record.
corrected_treatment: The research institution supports the second-century date of the Geography; local passages and geographical identifications remain unverified.

earlier_claim: Greek/Roman trade evidence shows early maritime connections.
corrected_treatment: Texts and ceramics support exchange; they do not prove all visiting or resident people were Roman, or settle every port coordinate.

earlier_claim: Kerala was formed on 1 November 1956.
corrected_treatment: Sections 2(a) and 5 of the 1956 Act support the appointed day.

earlier_claim: The modern physical landscape has developed over geological time.
corrected_treatment: Retain the distinction between basement history, topography, sedimentation and modern administrative boundaries.

earlier_claim: Earth formed approximately 4.54 billion years ago.
corrected_treatment: Use as global context only, not a local sample age.

earlier_claim: Southern Kerala includes an ancient crystalline geological foundation.
corrected_treatment: Relevant geochronology exists. Sample-level ages are not adopted until corrections and analytical context are checked.

earlier_claim: The oldest rock beneath Kerala has a single already-established age.
corrected_treatment: No oldest-material ranking was resolved. Separate measured ages, inherited grains and crustal model ages.

earlier_claim: Part I can end and Part II begin at 250 million years ago.
corrected_treatment: This is a proposed book division, not an observed Kerala-specific boundary. Replace with process-based dossiers.

earlier_claim: Trivandrum Block research is relevant to Gondwana assembly.
corrected_treatment: Retain the connection as the authors’ interpretation; full geochronological evaluation remains pending.

earlier_claim: Gondwana assembly and India’s later separations are the same episode.
corrected_treatment: Maintain separate assembly, rifting, separation and magmatism records.

earlier_claim: The western margin is related to continental breakup and tectono-magmatic processes.
corrected_treatment: Retain a multi-stage research framework; exact episode ages need additional primary studies.

earlier_claim: India–Madagascar separation has been precisely dated in this chat.
corrected_treatment: The earlier response proposed investigating its date; it did not verify a precise chronology.

earlier_claim: The Western Ghats were not made in one instantaneous event.
corrected_treatment: Separate relief, exhumation, erosion, magmatism and sedimentation rather than imposing a single birthday.

earlier_claim: Offshore basin sedimentation informs Western Ghats evolution.
corrected_treatment: Relevant paper confirmed; publication is 2008.

earlier_claim: Present backwaters, estuaries and river mouths have a single known formation date.
corrected_treatment: No local core-based reconstruction was completed. This remains a research dossier.

earlier_claim: Sea-level changes and sedimentation affected the coast.
corrected_treatment: Do not turn the general process framework into specific local dates without dated cores and geomorphology.

earlier_claim: Monsoon, biodiversity and forests can be narrated continuously from the geological start.
corrected_treatment: Retrieve independent palaeoclimate, fossil and ecological evidence before filling a continuous narrative.

earlier_claim: Palaeontology can be omitted from a complete land history.
corrected_treatment: Add fossil and sedimentary histories; the Quilon studies are a concrete initial source route.

earlier_claim: Northern Kerala has been occupied since the Lower Palaeolithic.
corrected_treatment: The accessible 2016 abstract suggests this. Full archaeological context and absolute dates are not reviewed.

earlier_claim: Early tool evidence dates the arrival of Homo sapiens specifically.
corrected_treatment: No species identification follows automatically from a stone-tool attribution. The local record needs separate biological evidence.

earlier_claim: Thenmala and Ankode are relevant Mesolithic sites.
corrected_treatment: The overview names them; primary reports and dating need inspection.

earlier_claim: The Mesolithic of Kerala is uniformly microlithic.
corrected_treatment: The cited overview explicitly describes a different local toolkit; preserve assemblage differences.

earlier_claim: A charcoal age of 5210 years ago can be converted directly to a BCE year.
corrected_treatment: Retrieve laboratory age, uncertainty and calibration; do not subtract from today or simply from 1950.

earlier_claim: Kerala’s Neolithic and farming transitions followed one fixed sequence.
corrected_treatment: The earlier caveat against uniformity is retained. Actual crop, animal and settlement evidence is still needed.

earlier_claim: A polished celt near Edakkal directly dates all the engravings.
corrected_treatment: Association alone is not secure absolute dating of each panel.

earlier_claim: All megaliths belong to one ethnic people or one synchronous culture.
corrected_treatment: Treat monuments, assemblages and dates individually. No ethnolinguistic identity is assigned from monument type.

earlier_claim: Iron, agriculture and social differentiation can be placed on one territory-wide timeline.
corrected_treatment: Separate evidence for metallurgy, crop production, residence and hierarchy; do not assume their simultaneity.

earlier_claim: Pattanam’s chronology can stand in for all of Kerala.
corrected_treatment: The approximate phases in the 2013 handbook are site-specific.

earlier_claim: Pattanam is conclusively Muziris.
corrected_treatment: Keep the archaeological site and the ancient textual toponym separate, linked by attributed identification hypotheses.

earlier_claim: The earliest Cheras, later Cheras and Chera Perumals are one continuous proven chronology.
corrected_treatment: The earlier outline named research topics, not a demonstrated dynastic continuity.

earlier_claim: The post-early-Chera transition can be filled with a neat continuous political narrative.
corrected_treatment: Record chronological disagreements and gaps; retrieve regional epigraphic and archaeological studies.

earlier_claim: Malayalam has an exact birth year.
corrected_treatment: No such year is supported. Language features, inscription classification and manuscript transmission need separate evidence.

earlier_claim: The earliest Malayalam inscription or its date was established here.
corrected_treatment: No ranking was audited. The Kollam project illustrates revised language attribution, not a settled first-inscription claim.

earlier_claim: Religious-community founding narratives directly date historical arrivals.
corrected_treatment: Retain traditions as attributed narratives; independent documents, buildings, artefacts and dated witnesses require separate records.

earlier_claim: Later caste and land relations existed unchanged in prehistory.
corrected_treatment: The earlier warning against anachronism stands; specific local developments remain to be researched.

earlier_claim: Medieval Kerala was a single unified kingdom.
corrected_treatment: Do not infer political unity from the study boundary. The powers listed earlier are topics requiring source-level verification.

earlier_claim: Arab and Chinese connections have been exhaustively documented in this chat.
corrected_treatment: The earlier outline provided topics, not a corpus audit. Build dated primary-text and object records.

earlier_claim: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498.
corrected_treatment: The journal extract supports the year. Exact day and calendar normalization remain separate checks.

earlier_claim: Portuguese arrival discovered a previously unknown trading coast.
corrected_treatment: Earlier trade is directly attested in the Periplus. Use arrival within an existing network, not discovery as an absolute.

earlier_claim: The detailed chronology of Dutch, Mysorean and British involvement was verified.
corrected_treatment: These were chapter topics, not checked event chronologies. Keep their documentary investigation in the work queue.

earlier_claim: British-administered Malabar and the princely states had identical arrangements.
corrected_treatment: The earlier distinction is a necessary research frame. This pass did not audit all administrative transitions.

earlier_claim: Mappila uprisings, Vaikom, temple entry, labour and independence developments were all verified.
corrected_treatment: The outline names them without evidentiary dossiers. Verify individual dates, actors, casualties and interpretations from contemporaneous records.

earlier_claim: 1947–1956 describes every integration event sufficiently.
corrected_treatment: Distinguish individual instruments and commencement dates; the outline is not a substitute for their legal history.

earlier_claim: All Travancore-Cochin entered the new state in 1956.
corrected_treatment: Section 4 transfers named taluks to Madras; section 5 concerns the remaining Travancore-Cochin territories.

earlier_claim: All Malabar district entered the new state in 1956.
corrected_treatment: Section 5 excludes Laccadive and Minicoy islands; read section 6 for the island territory.

earlier_claim: Kasaragod’s inclusion can be ignored in the 1956 summary.
corrected_treatment: Section 5 includes Kasaragod taluk of South Kanara.

earlier_claim: Historical Travancore, Malabar and modern Kerala are interchangeable areas.
corrected_treatment: Use a place-level temporal crosswalk. Outside places can still be included as explicit context.

earlier_claim: Mahe is part of the modern Kerala administrative scope.
corrected_treatment: The official district portal identifies the Puducherry administration; distinguish district territory from river basin.

earlier_claim: The 1956 Act fully defines a GIS boundary for today.
corrected_treatment: Acquire a licensed current polygon and audit later changes. This release does not contain verified geometry.

earlier_claim: Post-1956 politics, land reforms, health, migration and economic transformation are already fully verified.
corrected_treatment: These are research programmes in the earlier outline, not audited year-by-year findings.

earlier_claim: Parasurama tradition is a dated physical explanation of coastal formation.
corrected_treatment: Treat it as a textual/oral tradition with witnesses and reception history, not an empirical geological chronology.

earlier_claim: Ordinary people and environmental history should be separate optional add-ons.
corrected_treatment: Integrate livelihoods, gender, marginalized communities and environment into every relevant period, not only end chapters.

earlier_claim: The five previously linked resources were all full-text-verified.
corrected_treatment: They are real relevant leads with different inspection depths; two publisher articles and the NDLI article were not read in full.

earlier_claim: The earlier Trivandrum reference needs no corrections check.
corrected_treatment: An erratum was located and remains unread; do not claim its contents are harmless or decisive.

earlier_claim: A year embedded in a DOI is always the publication year.
corrected_treatment: The margin paper is 1998 and the Basin Research paper is 2008 despite misleading DOI digits.

earlier_claim: Publisher online-hosting dates always date the original study.
corrected_treatment: The Pattanam article is a 2004 publication with a 2015 hosting date. Preserve both fields.

earlier_claim: Abstracts, catalogues and full articles provide the same level of verification.
corrected_treatment: Record inspection depth. A catalogue can verify bibliographic identity but not unseen sample tables or text readings.

earlier_claim: Every year after writing begins necessarily has a surviving year-specific record.
corrected_treatment: Generate navigation pages without fabricating events. Interval evidence remains in canonical period records.

earlier_claim: No entry in a year file means nothing happened that year.
corrected_treatment: In this release it means no year-specific seed has yet been entered, not absence of events or surviving evidence.

earlier_claim: All online public material is free to republish under the repo license.
corrected_treatment: Index and paraphrase by default; record rights at item level, and rehost only with a defensible permission or public-domain determination.

earlier_claim: A finite search can establish exhaustive coverage of the whole changing web.
corrected_treatment: Pursue exhaustive inventory within declared collection snapshots and publish unknowns, access failures and missing ranges rather than an invented global percentage.

earlier_claim: Starting annual files at 300 BCE proves recorded history began in that year.
corrected_treatment: 300 BCE is the chosen start of the initial third-century navigation container. Earlier documentary evidence can extend it.

earlier_claim: The full project has been checked by independent historians or field specialists.
corrected_treatment: This release is AI-assisted and source-audited at the stated depths; human scholarly review is pending throughout.
